lesson.title: Save the widest sound for the end.
lesson.move: Keep bars 1–2 compact. In bars 3–4, lift the melody an octave and widen the chord register.
lesson.exercise:
Write 8 bars in A.
Keep bars 1–4 sparse.
Widen only bars 5–8.
Add sustain, not speed.
lesson.detail: A keeps the melody compact: C♯5–C♯5–B4–B4. B preserves bars 1–2, then lifts the B notes to B5 in bars 3–4 and adds upper chord tones in the piano and organ. The harmony, bass, tempo and attack positions stay fixed. This intentionally changes register and ensemble density. C♯, not E, is the common melody note across Dmaj7 and C♯m7. Dmaj7 contains D, F♯, A and C♯.
lesson.assignment: Write eight bars in A. In bars 1–4, use restrained three-note upper chords and one sustained melody note per bar. In bars 5–8, widen the register or add a complementary sustained voice without increasing the attack rate. Use C♯ as a real shared tone across Dmaj7 and C♯m7, and let E7sus4 resolve to the ending A chord.
